narrative:
The model determined that you have an 85% chance of representing a bad credit risk. This high probability led directly to the denial of your loan application.

The three factors that weighed most heavily in this decision were the size of the loan you requested, the length of time you wanted to repay it, and the status of your checking account. All three pushed the prediction strongly toward bad credit risk.

Your requested loan amount of 15,672 DM is more than five times higher than the average amount approved applicants ask for. This large sum significantly increased the model's concern about your ability to repay. Similarly, you asked for a 48-month repayment period, more than twice as long as the typical 19 months seen among approved applicants. Longer durations make repayment less certain in the model's view. Finally, having a checking account balance between 0 and 200 DM is relatively uncommon among successful applicants and also worked against you.

Taken together, these three factors created a clear picture of elevated risk for the bank. 

To improve your chances next time, consider applying for a substantially smaller loan with a shorter repayment period. Bringing your checking account balance above 200 DM before reapplying would also help demonstrate greater financial stability.
